findings.description: run_states() applies one global lock probe to every run id lacking a RunRecord, so while any nightly holds nightly.lock, every older interrupted run (killed before its RunRecord was written) is reported as in_progress instead of interrupted. Only the newest run without a RunRecord can be the live one; older ones are interrupted regardless of the lock. The results CLI and the runbook's 'interrupted vs in_progress' distinction therefore give wrong answers exactly during the window an operator is most likely to query (a run in flight). Suggested fix: when held, label only the most recent unfinished run id (by first-seen order or recorded_at) as in_progress and the rest interrupted.

findings.existing_code:
tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="gh-shim-")
    work = os.path.join(tmp, "r")
    git("clone", "-q", origin, work)
findings.description: merge_pr clones the bare origin into a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp directory and never removes it, on either the success or the failure path. Each `gh pr merge` the agent under test issues leaks a full clone under /tmp; a nightly suite running merge-pull-requests scenarios across several vendors leaks one per pair per night, and the nightly's own `_remove_workspace` cannot reclaim them because they live outside the workdir. Wrap the clone in try/finally with shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True), or place the clone under bin_dir_for(workdir) so existing workspace cleanup covers it.

The RunRecord written by finish() stores the configured vendor list, not the effective one. When a vendor is excluded by preflight (CLI unavailable, or the broken-vendor exclusion path that still leaves >=2 effective vendors), the run record claims vendors that never executed, so `results latest`/trend consumers and the runbook's 'which vendors ran' question read a misleading answer. Record the effective vendors (and optionally the excluded ones with a reason) so the ledger reflects what actually ran.

install_gh_shim is invoked for every live run, including fixtures without `local_remote`. The shim's gh-state.json then points `origin` at a bare repo path that was never created, so any `gh pr create`/`gh pr merge` the agent attempts will fail inside the shim with a git clone/push error rather than a clean 'unsupported call' entry in gh-unsupported.log; the scenario surfaces as a vendor error with an opaque traceback instead of the designed `gh shim: unsupported call` message. Either skip shim installation (or install a stub that logs every call as unsupported) when fx.local_remote is false, or have the shim check origin existence and route to the unsupported log.

findings.existing_code:
- Coordinator running at `COORDINATOR_URL` (default: http://localhost:8000)
- Falls back gracefully with a warning if the coordinator is unreachable
findings.description: The task-4.4a repair added `--agent-id`, `IMPROVE_HARNESS_AGENT_ID`, and `COORDINATION_API_KEY` (Bearer auth) to analyze_failures.py, and the live coordinator at COORDINATOR_URL now rejects unauthenticated /memory/query with 401 (which query_memory reports only as 'Coordinator unreachable' and returns []). SKILL.md's Prerequisites and Step 1 example still describe only COORDINATOR_URL and do not mention the key or agent id, so a user following the skill against a secured coordinator silently gets an empty ranking with a misleading 'unreachable' warning. Document COORDINATION_API_KEY / IMPROVE_HARNESS_AGENT_ID (and the `--agent-id` flag) in Prerequisites, and consider distinguishing HTTP 401/403 from a connection failure in the warning text.

The broken-skill acceptance test only exercises the improve-harness ranking assertion when skills/improve-harness/scripts/analyze_failures.py exists on disk; otherwise it silently passes without checking that the emitted capability-gap entries rank the broken skill first. Because this file lives at a fixed repo-relative path and the test is the acceptance evidence for design D3/D4 ('improve-harness surfaces the gap'), a rename or a packaging layout where the skills tree is absent turns the key assertion into a no-op green. Use pytest.skip with a reason (visible in the summary) or make the path a hard assertion so the gap is reported rather than hidden.

The shim's shebang interpolates sys.executable verbatim. Linux shebangs do not support spaces or quoting, so a venv under a path containing a space (common on dev laptops with `~/My Projects/...`) yields a shim that cannot be executed and every `gh` call fails with ENOENT-style errors rather than the designed unsupported-call path. Low likelihood in the nightly deployment (systemd unit, fixed path); if it matters, write a `#!/bin/sh` trampoline that execs "$PYTHON" "$0" with the path quoted, or exec via a tiny sh wrapper.

skills_sha() marks the sha `+dirty` from a repo-wide `git status --porcelain`, so any uncommitted file anywhere in the checkout (an unrelated worktree edit, a stray review-findings.json) flags the skills sha as dirty even when skills/ itself is clean. This matches the spec wording ('that checkout has uncommitted changes') so it is not a defect, but trend consumers comparing skills_sha across nights will see spurious dirty markers on a dev machine. Scoping the porcelain call to the skills directory (`git status --porcelain -- <skills_dir>`) would make the marker mean what readers assume.
